artworks.title: Nemesis
artworks.description: A painting by the German artist Alfred Rethel depicting the winged goddess of retribution in pursuit of a fleeing murderer, vengeance following inescapably across an open, desolate landscape. The work casts the ancient goddess in the brooding moral key of German Romanticism.

artworks.title: Nemesis (The Great Fortune)
artworks.description: A copperplate engraving by Albrecht Duerer, among the most celebrated prints of the Northern Renaissance. The winged goddess balances on a sphere high above an Alpine valley, holding a goblet and a bridle, emblems of the reward and the restraint she dispenses. Duerer fused Nemesis with the figure of Fortune, drawing on the humanist Poliziano's Latin poem 'Manto'; this impression is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, DC.

artworks.title: Nemesis of Rhamnous Type (Farnese)
artworks.description: Roman marble copy of the cult statue Agorakritos carved for Nemesis' sanctuary at Rhamnous in Attica. The goddess stands draped and measured — retribution as classical calm. Farnese Collection, Naples.

artworks.title: Nemesis (Rhamnous type)
artworks.description: Miniaturised Roman replica of the Rhamnous cult image — Nemesis reduced to a handheld scale of justice. National Gallery Prague, Kinský Palace.
